timeline.text: Artem's insulin dose used to be calculated from whatever numbers were already saved, even weeks old.
If his weight crept up and nobody noticed, the calculator kept dosing off the old numbers anyway, with no warning.
That's like trusting a scale you stepped on last month.
Now the save button stays locked until those numbers are confirmed fresh.
And if his weight shifts by more than 5 percent, it flags the risk before a dose goes out.
